items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: We had Yank Johnson on trombone, good trombone player.

ctx.x: What kind of music did he have Sam?

Soft, nothing barstress, tempo is great. Them guys were together. We had Yank Johnson on trombone, good trombone player. Joe Watson on clarinet and Guy on band. Eddie, get his name now. That time I seen him playing bass on him. Down in Alexander, Virginia. Little Eddie. Good bass volunteer. Did he have a nickname? No I always called him Eddie. And Alfred was playing trombone. Alfred Williams. Steady tempo. Yeah. They had a tempo man there. Well when them guys pull up on the corner they wouldn't buck, you know…
I wonder about that bass player, his name was Eddie huh? What other bands did he play with? Nah.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: We had Yank Johnson. On trombone.

ctx.x: What kind of music did he have, Sam?

Soft. Nothing boisterous. Tempo is big. And guys are together. We had Yank Johnson. On trombone. Good trombone, brother. Joe Watson on clarinet. Guy on paranger. Eddie. Get his name now. Next time I seen him playing bass on him. On Alexander, Virginia. Little Eddie. Little Eddie. Good bass violin player. Did he have a nickname? No, I always call him Eddie. And Alfred was playing drums.
